elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Retained § 14.1(A)(1) sets "primary limits of not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)" for CGL but does not state a per-occurrence limit; the undifferentiated "primary limits" figure cannot be read literally as a per-occurrence amount.[unverified]

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: The same retained CGL item gives a single $2,000,000 "primary limits" figure with no per-occurrence/aggregate split, so an aggregate limit of $2,000,000 is not expressly stated.[unverified]

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language provides "Professional Liability (Errors and Omissions) Insurance in an amount not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000)" — below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language provides "Cyber and Privacy Liability Insurance in an amount not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)" — below the preferred USD 5,000,000 for a data-processing provider.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Retained § 14.1(A)(3): "Workers' Compensation Insurance as mandated or allowed by the state in which the Services are being performed, including at least five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) coverage for Employer's Liability."

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Retained § 14.1(B): "annually thereafter, at Customer's request, M&I shall deliver to Customer original Certificates of Insurance evidencing the coverage required by this Section" — which by its terms picks up the newly added lines.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence in § 14.1(A): "Professional Liability (Errors and Omissions) Insurance in an amount not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000)", carried by the lead-in obligation "M&I shall maintain at all times at its own cost and expense" throughout the Term.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "Cyber and Privacy Liability Insurance in an amount not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000)"; the obligation is unconditional and not narrowed to selected data types.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: both fallback elements (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000) appear in operative, mandatory language inside the existing § 14.1(A) maintenance covenant.

Preferred is not complete: E&O is USD 1,000,000 (needs USD 2,000,000), cyber/privacy is USD 2,000,000 (needs USD 5,000,000), and the retained CGL item states only an undifferentiated USD 2,000,000 "primary limits" figure rather than the USD 1,000,000 per-occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate split. If the preferred level were targeted, the drafter would need to restate CGL as "$1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate" and raise the two new limits.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single appended coverage line; nothing was deleted or paraphrased, favourable existing terms (fidelity $10M, workers' comp, all-risk property, A-rated carriers, 30 days' notice, certificates) survive verbatim, and no extras were added — no separate at-own-expense clause (the § 14.1(A) lead-in already supplies it), no survival tail, no new procedures, and the fallback thresholds were not exceeded.

Intent preserved: the certificate mechanic in § 14.1(B) refers to "the coverage required by this Section" and therefore extends to the new lines without duplication; no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in the checklist elements): the inserted coverage line is appended without a list number in an otherwise numbered list (1.–4.); numbering it "5." would tidy the insertion without changing substance.
